punchline: Goggins trained twenty minutes every other day, ran 101 miles, broke bones in his feet and still says the mind quits early.
thirty_sec: In 2005 David Goggins signed up for a 24-hour race in San Diego with almost no preparation. He ran 101 miles in about nineteen hours, broke bones in his feet and passed blood afterwards. He reads such moments through his 40% Rule: when your mind says you are done, you are only about 40 percent done. It is his own rule of thumb, not a measurement.
